summary: Verified the rewarded-ad -> PDF download bug fix in RewardedAdDialog.jsx. The primary reported bug ('après avoir vu la vidéo le téléchargement ne se fait pas') is FIXED. Ran the full ad watch->download flow twice consecutively; both attempts produced a browser download event with filename FAC-2026-001.pdf (~276 KB each). Cancel path closes the dialog without triggering a download. Regression: the invoice is auto-saved to Historique after each ad-gated download (FAC-2026-001 visible in the history side panel).
critical_code_review_comments: RewardedAdDialog.jsx: legacy timerRef/clearInterval branch in clearTimer() is now dead code because the countdown is effect-driven (only clearTimeout of the per-tick timer is used). Minor cleanup opportunity, not a bug.

grantReward() sets a setTimeout(1100ms) but has no cleanup if the dialog is closed manually during 'granted' phase — currently harmless because rewardedRef guards double invocation, but the 1100ms fallback timer is not tracked in the unmount cleanup path (only via clearTimer on close/unmount, which does clear it — OK).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Bug fully validated on public preview URL. Playwright expect_download confirms browser download event fires after the 5s simulated countdown + 1.1s grant delay. StrictMode double-mount no longer cancels the reward. Repeat runs (x2) both succeeded with identical filename. History regression also confirmed.
rca of the issue: Original bug: countdown used setInterval + called grantReward()/setTimeout(onReward) from *inside* a setRemaining updater. React 18 StrictMode invokes state updater functions twice for reasoning; the second (discarded) invocation still executed the side effect, scheduling a second grant timeout and clearing/resetting refs so onReward() was never called or was cancelled. Fix moved the timer into a useEffect keyed on [phase, remaining] and made grantReward idempotent via rewardedRef; onReward now fires deterministically ~1.1s after the countdown reaches 0.
